title: Baby Maths: Posting & Containers
strapline: In, out, fill, tip — the first maths is the maths of putting things in things.
intent: Babies explore filling and emptying — the deep, repeated schema behind later ideas of quantity and capacity.
Babies discover 'in' and 'out', 'gone' and 'back again', building the roots of number and object permanence.
Babies refine reaching, grasping, releasing and posting — the hand control that maths tools later need.
Babies experience one-to-one correspondence in the body — one object, one posting slot, one plop.
Babies share the delight of cause and effect with a warm adult who names what happens.
implementation: Offer open baskets and containers with collections of safe objects — wooden balls, scarves, pine cones, big beads.
Include posting toys and home-made ones — a tub with a hole in the lid, a tissue box, a slotted pot.
Follow the baby's lead: let them fill, tip out and start again as many times as they like — the repetition is the learning.
Narrate simply and warmly: 'in it goes... all gone... here it is again!'
Sit close and hand objects back, keeping the game going and the connection alive.
Rotate the objects and containers to keep the schema fresh — different sizes, sounds and textures.
Keep everything larger than a choke-tester and check the collection often for safety.
key_questions: In it goes — where did it go?
Shall we fill it right up?
What happens when you tip it out?
Have you got another one to post?

impact.text: Babies fill and empty containers over and over with growing purpose.
Babies post objects into slots, refining aim and release.
Babies explore 'gone' and 'back again', building object permanence.
Babies reach, grasp and let go with increasing control.
Babies share the game with an adult, taking turns to give and take.

enhancements: Home-made posting boxes — a tub with a slot, a colander with pipe cleaners.
Treasure baskets of natural objects to fill and tip.
Nesting cups and stacking pots that fit inside one another.
Fabric scarves in a tissue box to pull out one by one.
A shallow tray of larger dry pasta shells to scoop with a cup.
Different-sounding containers — a metal tin, a wooden bowl — for the plop and clatter.

playing_exploring: Babies explore filling and emptying freely, at their own pace.
They mouth, shake and post to find out what each object does.
active_learning: Babies repeat the same fill-and-tip action many times, deeply absorbed.
creating_thinking: Babies begin to expect the object to reappear, anticipating the outcome.
